core: Non-devotional, descriptive, and analytical academic study

claims.claim: The AAR's college religious-literacy guidelines distinguish confessional or prescriptive statements from descriptive or analytical statements.
Academic Religious Studies draws on a range of disciplinary methodologies rather than a single method.
Participant observation combines participation in a setting with observation and records.
Researchers should attend to the rights of people who provide information and to the effect of documentation on a setting.
Ethnographic inquiry seeks to understand practices and meanings in context and requires attention to bias.
A comparison is strongest when it states its basis, preserves contextual differences, and limits its conclusion to the available evidence.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The generated draft offered generic study-skills language, a non-specific definition, and incomplete three-option questions without source support.
correctionsNeeded: Replaced boilerplate with a neutral explanation of academic inquiry.
Added source- and context-aware methods, including limits on observation and comparison.
Added five four-option questions with varied cognitive demands and evidence support.
rightsIssues: The AAR and OpenStax materials were used for fact checking and synthesis only. No source prose was reproduced.

sourceRecords.title: AAR Religious Literacy Guidelines
sourceRecords.notes: Read as a Tier A professional-association guideline for college teaching. Supports the distinction between confessional or prescriptive and descriptive or analytical statements and the academic study of religion's methodological range. Reference only; original prose.

sourceRecords.title: 2.4 Participant Observation and Interviewing — Introduction to Anthropology
sourceRecords.notes: Read as a Tier B OER source. Supports the description of participant observation, interviewing, records, informant rights, and care about documenting a setting. Reference only; original prose.

sourceRecords.title: 2.3 Ethnography and Ethnology — Introduction to Anthropology
sourceRecords.notes: Read as a Tier B OER source. Supports contextual ethnographic inquiry and the need to attend to bias when studying a culture. Reference only; original prose.
